@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+---
+name: "jupyter-notebook"
+description: "Use when the user asks to create, scaffold, or edit Jupyter notebooks (`.ipynb`) for experiments, explorations, or tutorials; prefer the bundled templates and run the helper script `new_notebook.py` to generate a clean starting notebook."
+---
+
+
+# Jupyter Notebook Skill
+
+Create clean, reproducible Jupyter notebooks for two primary modes:
+
+- Experiments and exploratory analysis
+- Tutorials and teaching-oriented walkthroughs
+
+Prefer the bundled templates and the helper script for consistent structure and fewer JSON mistakes.
+
+## When to use
+- Create a new `.ipynb` notebook from scratch.
+- Convert rough notes or scripts into a structured notebook.
+- Refactor an existing notebook to be more reproducible and skimmable.
+- Build experiments or tutorials that will be read or re-run by other people.
+
+## Decision tree
+- If the request is exploratory, analytical, or hypothesis-driven, choose `experiment`.
+- If the request is instructional, step-by-step, or audience-specific, choose `tutorial`.
+- If editing an existing notebook, treat it as a refactor: preserve intent and improve structure.
+
+## Skill path (set once)
+
+```bash
+export CODEX_HOME="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}"
+export JUPYTER_NOTEBOOK_CLI="$CODEX_HOME/skills/jupyter-notebook/scripts/new_notebook.py"
+```
+
+User-scoped skills install under `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (default: `~/.codex/skills`).
+
+## Workflow
+1. Lock the intent.
+Identify the notebook kind: `experiment` or `tutorial`.
+Capture the objective, audience, and what "done" looks like.
+
+2. Scaffold from the template.
+Use the helper script to avoid hand-authoring raw notebook JSON.
+
+```bash
+uv run --python 3.12 python "$JUPYTER_NOTEBOOK_CLI" \
+  --kind experiment \
+  --title "Compare prompt variants" \
+  --out output/jupyter-notebook/compare-prompt-variants.ipynb
+```
+
+```bash
+uv run --python 3.12 python "$JUPYTER_NOTEBOOK_CLI" \
+  --kind tutorial \
+  --title "Intro to embeddings" \
+  --out output/jupyter-notebook/intro-to-embeddings.ipynb
+```
+
+3. Fill the notebook with small, runnable steps.
+Keep each code cell focused on one step.
+Add short markdown cells that explain the purpose and expected result.
+Avoid large, noisy outputs when a short summary works.
+
+4. Apply the right pattern.
+For experiments, follow `references/experiment-patterns.md`.
+For tutorials, follow `references/tutorial-patterns.md`.
+
+5. Edit safely when working with existing notebooks.
+Preserve the notebook structure; avoid reordering cells unless it improves the top-to-bottom story.
+Prefer targeted edits over full rewrites.
+If you must edit raw JSON, review `references/notebook-structure.md` first.
+
+6. Validate the result.
+Run the notebook top-to-bottom when the environment allows.
+If execution is not possible, say so explicitly and call out how to validate locally.
+Use the final pass checklist in `references/quality-checklist.md`.
+
+## Templates and helper script
+- Templates live in `assets/experiment-template.ipynb` and `assets/tutorial-template.ipynb`.
+- The helper script loads a template, updates the title cell, and writes a notebook.
+
+Script path:
+- `$JUPYTER_NOTEBOOK_CLI` (installed default: `$CODEX_HOME/skills/jupyter-notebook/scripts/new_notebook.py`)
+
+## Temp and output conventions
+- Use `tmp/jupyter-notebook/` for intermediate files; delete when done.
+- Write final artifacts under `output/jupyter-notebook/` when working in this repo.
+- Use stable, descriptive filenames (for example, `ablation-temperature.ipynb`).
+
+## Dependencies (install only when needed)
+Prefer `uv` for dependency management.
+
+Optional Python packages for local notebook execution:
+
+```bash
+uv pip install jupyterlab ipykernel
+```
+
+The bundled scaffold script uses only the Python standard library and does not require extra dependencies.
+
+## Environment
+No required environment variables.
+
+## Reference map
+- `references/experiment-patterns.md`: experiment structure and heuristics.
+- `references/tutorial-patterns.md`: tutorial structure and teaching flow.
+- `references/notebook-structure.md`: notebook JSON shape and safe editing rules.
+- `references/quality-checklist.md`: final validation checklist.

+{
+  "cells": [
+    {
+      "cell_type": "markdown",
+      "metadata": {},
+      "source": [
+        "# Experiment: TITLE\n",
+        "\n",
+        "Objective:\n",
+        "- State the question you want to answer.\n",
+        "- Define the success criteria.\n"
+      ]
+    },
+    {
+      "cell_type": "code",
+      "execution_count": null,
+      "metadata": {},
+      "outputs": [],
+      "source": [
+        "# Setup: imports and reproducibility\n",
+        "from __future__ import annotations\n",
+        "\n",
+        "import random\n",
+        "import statistics\n",
+        "\n",
+        "SEED = 7\n",
+        "random.seed(SEED)\n",
+        "SEED\n"
+      ]
+    },
+    {
+      "cell_type": "markdown",
+      "metadata": {},
+      "source": [
+        "## Plan\n",
+        "\n",
+        "- Hypothesis:\n",
+        "- Variables to sweep:\n",
+        "- Metrics to record:\n"
+      ]
+    },
+    {
+      "cell_type": "code",
+      "execution_count": null,
+      "metadata": {},
+      "outputs": [],
+      "source": [
+        "# Define parameters and lightweight helpers\n",
+        "sample_size = 20\n",
+        "values = [random.random() for _ in range(sample_size)]\n",
+        "summary = {\n",
+        "    \"count\": len(values),\n",
+        "    \"mean\": statistics.fmean(values),\n",
+        "    \"min\": min(values),\n",
+        "    \"max\": max(values),\n",
+        "}\n",
+        "summary\n"
+      ]
+    },
+    {
+      "cell_type": "markdown",
+      "metadata": {},
+      "source": [
+        "## Results\n",
+        "\n",
+        "- Key observations:\n",
+        "- Surprises or failure modes:\n",
+        "- Decision: continue, pivot, or stop:\n"
+      ]
+    },
+    {
+      "cell_type": "code",
+      "execution_count": null,
+      "metadata": {},
+      "outputs": [],
+      "source": [
+        "# Record findings in a minimal, copy-pasteable structure\n",
+        "result = {\n",
+        "    \"seed\": SEED,\n",
+        "    \"mean\": summary[\"mean\"],\n",
+        "    \"range\": summary[\"max\"] - summary[\"min\"],\n",
+        "}\n",
+        "result\n"
+      ]
+    },
+    {
+      "cell_type": "markdown",
+      "metadata": {},
+      "source": [
+        "## Next steps\n",
+        "\n",
+        "- What to try next:\n",
+        "- What to document elsewhere (PRD, notes, issue):\n"
+      ]
+    }
+  ],
+  "metadata": {
+    "kernelspec": {
+      "display_name": "Python 3",

+# Experiment Patterns
+
+Use this structure for exploratory and experimental work:
+
+- Title and objective: state the question and the success criteria.
+- Setup and reproducibility: import only what you need, set a seed early, and keep configuration in one short cell.
+- Plan: list hypotheses, sweeps, and metrics before running code.
+- Minimal baseline: start with the smallest runnable example and confirm it runs end-to-end before adding complexity.
+- Results and notes: summarize findings in markdown near the relevant code and record key metrics in a small dictionary or table-like structure.
+- Next steps: decide whether to continue, pivot, or stop, and capture follow-up ideas as short bullets.

+# Notebook Structure
+
+Jupyter notebooks are JSON documents with this high-level shape:
+
+- `nbformat` and `nbformat_minor`
+- `metadata`
+- `cells` (a list of markdown and code cells)
+
+When editing `.ipynb` files programmatically:
+
+- Preserve `nbformat` and `nbformat_minor` from the template.
+- Keep `cells` as an ordered list; do not reorder unless intentional.
+- For code cells, set `execution_count` to `null` when unknown.
+- For code cells, set `outputs` to an empty list when scaffolding.
+- For markdown cells, keep `cell_type="markdown"` and `metadata={}`.
+
+Prefer scaffolding from the bundled templates or `new_notebook.py` (for example, `$CODEX_HOME/skills/jupyter-notebook/scripts/new_notebook.py`) instead of hand-authoring raw notebook JSON.

+# Quality Checklist
+
+Before delivering a notebook:
+
+- Run it top-to-bottom at least once (or as much as the environment allows).
+- Ensure early cells set all required state; avoid hidden state from prior runs.
+- Keep outputs tidy. Avoid giant outputs when a short summary works.
+- Prefer small tables, key metrics, or short printouts.
+- Keep the narrative skimmable. Use headings and short bullets, and avoid long paragraphs.
+- Leave helpful TODOs only when necessary, and label them clearly.
+- If execution is not possible, call out the risk and how to validate locally.

+# Tutorial Patterns
+
+Use this structure for teaching and walkthroughs:
+
+- Audience, prerequisites, and learning goals: say who it is for, list what they should already know, and state what they will be able to do by the end.
+- Outline: provide a short numbered outline so readers can skim.
+- Step-by-step flow: pair a short markdown explanation with a small code cell that runs on its own and a brief interpretation of the result.
+- Exercises: include at least one exercise that reinforces the key concept and provide an answer scaffold in the next cell.
+- Pitfalls and extensions: call out one common mistake and how to fix it, and suggest one optional extension for curious readers.

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+
+def slugify(text: str) -> str:
+    lowered = text.strip().lower()
+    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", lowered)
+    collapsed = re.sub(r"-+", "-", cleaned).strip("-")
+    return collapsed or "notebook"
+
+
+def find_repo_root(start: Path) -> Path:
+    for candidate in (start, *start.parents):
+        if (candidate / ".git").exists():
+            return candidate
+    return start
+
+
+def load_template(skill_dir: Path, kind: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    asset_name = "experiment-template.ipynb" if kind == "experiment" else "tutorial-template.ipynb"
+    template_path = skill_dir / "assets" / asset_name
+    if not template_path.exists():
+        raise SystemExit(f"Missing template: {template_path}")
+    with template_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        data = json.load(f)
+    if not isinstance(data, dict):
+        raise SystemExit(f"Unexpected template shape: {template_path}")
+    return data
+
+
+def update_title(notebook: dict[str, Any], kind: str, title: str) -> None:
+    prefix = "Experiment" if kind == "experiment" else "Tutorial"
+    expected = f"# {prefix}: {title}\n"
+
+    cells = notebook.get("cells")
+    if not isinstance(cells, list) or not cells:
+        raise SystemExit("Template notebook has no cells")
+
+    first_cell = cells[0]
+    if not isinstance(first_cell, dict) or first_cell.get("cell_type") != "markdown":
+        raise SystemExit("Template notebook must start with a markdown title cell")
+
+    source = first_cell.get("source", [])
+    if isinstance(source, str):
+        source_lines = [source]
+    elif isinstance(source, list):
+        source_lines = [str(line) for line in source]
+    else:
+        source_lines = []
+
+    if source_lines:
+        source_lines[0] = expected
+    else:
+        source_lines = [expected]
+
+    first_cell["source"] = source_lines
+
+    metadata = notebook.setdefault("metadata", {})
+    if not isinstance(metadata, dict):
+        raise SystemExit("Notebook metadata must be a mapping")
+
+    language_info = metadata.setdefault("language_info", {})
+    if isinstance(language_info, dict):
+        language_info.setdefault("name", "python")
+        language_info.setdefault("version", "3.12")
+
+
+def default_output(repo_root: Path, title: str) -> Path:
+    filename = f"{slugify(title)}.ipynb"
+    return repo_root / "output" / "jupyter-notebook" / filename
+
+
+def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Scaffold a Jupyter notebook for experiments or tutorials.")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--kind",
+        choices=["experiment", "tutorial"],
+        default="experiment",
+        help="Notebook style to scaffold (default: experiment).",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--title",
+        required=True,
+        help="Human-readable notebook title used in the first markdown cell.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--out",
+        type=Path,
+        default=None,
+        help="Output path for the notebook. Defaults to output/jupyter-notebook/<slug>.ipynb.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--force",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Overwrite the output file if it already exists.",
+    )
+    return parser.parse_args()
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    args = parse_args()
+
+    script_path = Path(__file__).resolve()
+    skill_dir = script_path.parents[1]
+    repo_root = find_repo_root(skill_dir)
+
+    notebook = load_template(skill_dir, args.kind)
+    update_title(notebook, args.kind, args.title)
+
+    out_path = args.out or default_output(repo_root, args.title)
+    out_path = out_path.resolve()
+
+    if out_path.exists() and not args.force:
+        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite existing file without --force: {out_path}")
+
+    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    with out_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        json.dump(notebook, f, indent=2)
+        f.write("\n")
+
+    print(f"Wrote {out_path} using kind={args.kind}.")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Group-level NARPS Hypothesis 1 analysis of fixed AO86 participant maps.
+
+Run from the workspace root with the supplied Python environment:
+  python analysis.py --permutations 5000 --seed 20261016
+
+Uses a one-sample random-effects t statistic and participant sign-flip max-T
+permutation inference (one-sided; whole-brain voxelwise FWE). The supplied
+maps are first-level contrast estimates, not t/z maps.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import platform
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
+import nibabel as nib
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+import scipy
+from scipy import ndimage
+from scipy.stats import t as student_t
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+INPUT = ROOT / "input"
+OUT = ROOT / "results"
+FIG = OUT / "figures"
+VM_PFC = {"x_min": -20, "x_max": 20, "y_min": 20, "y_max": 60,
+          "z_min": -20, "z_max": 20}
+
+
+def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as f:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            h.update(chunk)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def main(n_perm: int, seed: int, chunk_size: int) -> None:
+    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    FIG.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    sources = json.loads((INPUT / "sources.json").read_text())
+    participants = pd.read_csv(INPUT / "participants.tsv", sep="\t")
+    expected_ids = set(participants.participant_id)
+    files = sorted((INPUT / "data").glob("*_hypo1_cope.nii.gz"))
+    if len(files) != 54 or {p.name.split("_")[0] for p in files} != expected_ids:
+        raise RuntimeError("Map count/participant IDs do not match the pinned cohort table")
+
+    data = []
+    images = []
+    checks = []
+    for path in files:
+        key = path.relative_to(INPUT).as_posix()
+        expected = sources["files"][key]
+        actual_hash = sha256(path)
+        if path.stat().st_size != expected["bytes"] or actual_hash != expected["sha256"]:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Checksum or byte-size mismatch: {key}")
+        img = nib.load(str(path))
+        arr = img.get_fdata(dtype=np.float32)
+        if not np.isfinite(arr).all():
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Non-finite values in {key}")
+        data.append(arr)
+        images.append(img)
+        checks.append({"file": key, "bytes": path.stat().st_size, "sha256": actual_hash})
+
+    ref = images[0]
+    if any(a.shape != ref.shape or not np.allclose(a.affine, ref.affine) for a in images):
+        raise RuntimeError("Maps do not share an identical voxel grid")
+    X4 = np.stack(data, axis=0)
+    n = X4.shape[0]
+    # Values equal to zero encode out-of-estimation-mask voxels in these maps.
+    # A common support avoids treating such absent values as observed zeros.
+    mask = np.all(X4 != 0, axis=0)
+    if not mask.any():
+        raise RuntimeError("No common map support")
+    X = X4[:, mask].T.astype(np.float64, copy=False)  # voxels x participants
+    mean = X.mean(axis=1)
+    sd = X.std(axis=1, ddof=1)
+    t_obs = mean / (sd / np.sqrt(n))
+    p_unc = student_t.sf(t_obs, n - 1)
+
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    sumsq = np.sum(X * X, axis=1)
+    max_null = np.empty(n_perm, dtype=np.float32)
+    for start in range(0, n_perm, chunk_size):
+        stop = min(start + chunk_size, n_perm)
+        signs = rng.choice(np.array([-1.0, 1.0], dtype=np.float32),
+                           size=(stop - start, n), replace=True)
+        signed_sums = signs @ X.T.astype(np.float32, copy=False)
+        denominator = np.sqrt(np.maximum(n * sumsq[None, :] - signed_sums ** 2, 1e-20))
+        t_perm = signed_sums * np.sqrt(n - 1) / denominator
+        max_null[start:stop] = t_perm.max(axis=1)
+    observed_max = float(np.max(t_obs))
+    exceed = int(np.sum(max_null >= observed_max))

+"""Prepare one reviewed browsable copy; only coordinator files are authored."""
+from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
+import hashlib, json, os, shutil, stat, subprocess, sys, traceback
+
+config_path = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
+cfg = json.loads(config_path.read_text())
+root = Path(cfg['root']); repo = root / 'publisher'; repo.mkdir()
+main = Path('/Users/johnlee/code/CON/stamped-in-practice')
+pixi = ['pixi', 'run', '--manifest-path', str(main/'pixi.toml'), '--locked']
+host = json.loads(Path('/Users/johnlee/.config/stamped-in-practice/launch-neutral.json').read_text())
+canonical = cfg['canonical']; commands = []
+assert cfg['run_id'] != 'narps-neutral-r1-20'
+
+def sha(path):
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open('rb') as stream:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024*1024), b''): h.update(chunk)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+def save(path, value): path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True)+'\n')
+
+def run(argv, allow=False):
+    p = subprocess.run(list(map(str, argv)), cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
+    commands.append({'argv':list(map(str, argv)), 'cwd':str(repo), 'returncode':p.returncode,
+                     'stdout':p.stdout, 'stderr':p.stderr})
+    save(root/'commands-prepare.json', commands)
+    if not allow: p.check_returncode()
+    return p
+
+try:
+    plan_path = Path(cfg['plan_path']); assert sha(plan_path) == cfg['plan_sha256']
+    plan = json.loads(plan_path.read_text()); capture = Path(plan['capture_manifest']['path'])
+    assert plan['run_id'] == cfg['run_id'] == canonical['run_id']
+    assert sha(capture) == plan['capture_manifest']['sha256'] == canonical['capture_sha256']
+    assert plan['original_worker_head'] == canonical['worker_head_commit']
+    source_entries = {e['path']:e for e in json.loads(capture.read_text())['entries']}
+    inputs_path = Path(cfg['input_manifest_path']); route_path = Path(cfg['input_route_proof_path'])
+    assert sha(inputs_path) == cfg['input_manifest_sha256']
+    assert sha(route_path) == cfg['input_route_proof_sha256']
+    inputs = json.loads(inputs_path.read_text()); route = json.loads(route_path.read_text())
+    assert route['verified'] and route['input_files_verified'] == len(inputs['files']) == 58
+    assert route['input_manifest_sha256'] == cfg['input_manifest_sha256']
+    assert inputs['input_tree'] == canonical['input_tree']
+    run(['git','init','--initial-branch',cfg['branch']])
+    run(['git','remote','add','origin','git@github.com:leej3/stamped-in-practice.git'])
+    run(['git','config','remote.origin.annex-ignore','true'])
+    run(['git','fetch','--no-tags','origin',canonical['commit']])
+    run(['git','reset','--hard','FETCH_HEAD'])
+    assert run(['git','rev-parse','HEAD']).stdout.strip() == canonical['commit']
+    assert not (repo/'.git/objects/info/alternates').exists()
+    assert run(['git','rev-parse','HEAD:input']).stdout.strip() == inputs['input_tree']
+    assert run(['git','rev-parse',canonical['worker_head_commit']+':input']).stdout.strip() == inputs['input_tree']
+    run(['git','merge-base','--is-ancestor',canonical['worker_head_commit'],'HEAD'])
+    assert sha(repo/'coordinator/original-manifest.json') == canonical['capture_sha256']
+    assert sha(repo/'coordinator/delivery-01/index.json') == canonical['package_index_sha256']
+    archive_tree = run(['git','ls-tree','HEAD','coordinator/delivery-01/delivery.tar.gz']).stdout
+    original_readme = run(['git','ls-tree','HEAD','README.md']).stdout
+    run(pixi+['git','annex','init',cfg['run_id']+' browsable coordinator copy'])
+    run(['git','remote','add',host['annex_remote'],host['annex_git_url']])
+    run(['git','config','remote.'+host['annex_remote']+'.annexurl',host['annex_url']])
+    run(['git','fetch','origin','git-annex:refs/remotes/origin/git-annex'])
+    run(pixi+['git','annex','merge'])
+    assert run(['git','rev-parse','HEAD']).stdout.strip() == canonical['commit']
+    # Preflight the complete reviewed plan before copying any original files.
+    for e in plan['entries']:
+        path = PurePosixPath(e['path']); assert not path.is_absolute() and '..' not in path.parts
+        assert not any(c in e['path'] for c in '\n\r\0*?[]'), 'Unreviewed attribute pattern'
+        assert e['capture_path'] == 'content/workspace/'+e['path']
+        source = source_entries[e['capture_path']]
+        assert all(source.get(k) == e.get(k) for k in ['kind','mode','sha256','size','target'])
+        assert e['action'] in ['directory-no-placeholder','copy-to-git','copy-to-annex','preserve-literal-link']
+        dest = repo/e['path']; src = capture.parent/e['capture_path']
+        assert not dest.exists() and not dest.is_symlink(), 'Publisher collision: '+e['path']
+        assert stat.S_IMODE(src.lstat().st_mode) == e['mode']
+        if e['kind'] == 'file':
+            assert stat.S_ISREG(src.lstat().st_mode) and sha(src) == e['sha256'] and src.stat().st_size == e['size']
+        elif e['kind'] == 'symlink': assert os.readlink(src) == e['target']
+        else: assert e['kind'] == 'directory' and stat.S_ISDIR(src.lstat().st_mode)
+    copied = []
+    for e in plan['entries']:
+        if e['action'] == 'directory-no-placeholder': continue
+        dest = repo/e['path']; src = capture.parent/e['capture_path']; dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        row = {'original_path':e['path'],'published_path':e['path'],'kind':e['kind'],'source_mode':e['mode']}
+        if e['kind'] == 'symlink':
+            os.symlink(e['target'], dest); row.update(storage='literal-link',target=e['target'])
+        else:
+            with src.open('rb') as source, dest.open('xb') as target: shutil.copyfileobj(source,target)
+            os.chmod(dest,e['mode']); assert sha(dest) == sha(src) == e['sha256']
+            row.update(bytes=e['size'],sha256=e['sha256'],storage='annex' if e['action']=='copy-to-annex' else 'git')
+        copied.append(row)
+    with (repo/'.gitattributes').open('a') as stream:
+        stream.write('\n# Coordinator presentation copies; original scientific bytes unchanged.\n')
+        for e in copied:
+            stream.write(json.dumps('/'+e['published_path'])+' annex.largefiles='+('anything annex.backend=SHA256E' if e['storage']=='annex' else 'nothing')+'\n')
+    annex = [e['published_path'] for e in copied if e['storage']=='annex']
+    if annex: run(pixi+['git','annex','add','--force-large','--backend=SHA256E','--',*annex])
+    for e in copied:
+        if e['storage']=='annex': e['annex_key']=run(pixi+['git','annex','lookupkey',e['published_path']]).stdout.strip()
+    evidence = repo/'coordinator/browsable-copy-01'; evidence.mkdir()
+    shutil.copy2(plan_path,evidence/'plan.json'); shutil.copy2(inputs_path,evidence/'input-manifest.json')
+    shutil.copy2(route_path,evidence/'shared-input-route-proof.json'); shutil.copy2(config_path,evidence/'config.json')
+    shutil.copy2(Path(__file__),evidence/'prepare.py')
+    manifest = {'schema':'coordinator-browsable-copy-v1','run_id':cfg['run_id'],'parent_commit':canonical['commit'],
+      'source_worker_head':plan['original_worker_head'],'capture_sha256':sha(capture),'plan_sha256':sha(plan_path),
+      'copied_files':copied,'authoritative_archive':'../delivery-01/delivery.tar.gz','authoritative_capture':'../original-manifest.json',
+      'attribution':'Coordinator presentation copies of exact original stopped files; no worker credit or scientific execution.',
+      'source_files_unchanged':True,'scientific_execution':False,'input_tree':inputs['input_tree'],
+      'shared_input_route_proof_sha256':sha(route_path),'shared_input_manifest_sha256':sha(inputs_path),
+      'shared_input_route_published_commit':cfg['input_route_published_proof_commit'],
+      'input_verification_scope':'Exact Git input tree matches prior independently retrieved 58-payload input manifest; payloads not redundantly downloaded for this presentation.',
+      'mode_scope':'Original full modes retained here and in authoritative archive; Git preserves executable bits and literal links, annex preserves payload bytes.'}
+    save(evidence/'manifest.json',manifest)
+    with (repo/'coordinator/README.md').open('a') as stream:
+        stream.write('\n## Browsable original files\n\nOriginal scientific files are also available at their unchanged workspace paths. '
+          'The [copy manifest](browsable-copy-01/manifest.json) records exact source hashes, original modes and storage choices. '
+          'These are coordinator presentation copies; the complete archive remains authoritative. '
+          'The input tree matches the [shared retrieval proof](browsable-copy-01/shared-input-route-proof.json); '
+          'its 58 payloads were independently retrieved in the cited run 20 check. '
+          'No scientific execution or worker credit is implied.\n')
+    cmd=pixi+['pre-commit','run','--config',str(main/'.pre-commit-config.yaml'),'snapper','--files','coordinator/README.md']
+    if run(cmd,allow=True).returncode: run(cmd)
+    run(['git','add','--force','--','.gitattributes','coordinator/README.md','coordinator/browsable-copy-01',*[e['published_path'] for e in copied]])
+    run(['git','diff','--cached','--check','--','.gitattributes','coordinator'])
+    assert run(['git','diff','--cached','--name-only','--','input','coordinator/delivery-01','coordinator/original-manifest.json']).stdout == ''
+    for e in copied:
+        path=e['published_path']; mode=run(['git','ls-files','--stage','--',path]).stdout.split()[0]
+        expected='120000' if e['storage'] in ['annex','literal-link'] else ('100755' if e['source_mode']&0o111 else '100644')
+        assert mode == expected
+        if e['kind']=='file': assert sha(repo/path) == e['sha256']
+        else: assert os.readlink(repo/path) == e['target']
+    assert sha(capture) == canonical['capture_sha256']
+    assert run(['git','ls-tree','HEAD','coordinator/delivery-01/delivery.tar.gz']).stdout == archive_tree
+    if not any(e['published_path']=='README.md' for e in copied):
+        assert run(['git','ls-tree','HEAD','README.md']).stdout == original_readme
+    diff=run(['git','diff','--cached','--stat']).stdout; (root/'prepared-diff-stat.txt').write_text(diff)
+    (root/'prepared.patch').write_text(run(['git','diff','--cached','--binary']).stdout)
+    save(root/'prepared.json',dict(manifest,publisher=str(repo),branch=cfg['branch'],annex_files=annex,
+       package_index_sha256=canonical['package_index_sha256'],plan_path=str(plan_path),config_sha256=sha(config_path)))
+    print(json.dumps({'prepared':True,'run_id':cfg['run_id'],'files':len(copied),'annex_files':len(annex),'committed':False}))
+except BaseException:
+    (root/'failure-prepare.txt').write_text(traceback.format_exc()); raise

+# Potential gain and brain activity in the NARPS equal-indifference group
+
+## Question and result
+
+We tested the original NARPS Hypothesis 1: whether greater potential gains are associated with a positive fMRI response in ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) in the equal-indifference group. A whole-brain, one-sided max-statistic permutation test found corrected positive effects somewhere in the brain (peak *t*(53) = 6.62, MNI [−26, −102, −4], max-T FWE *p* = .0010; 24 voxels exceeded the corrected threshold). However, no whole-brain FWE-significant voxels fell in the prespecified vmPFC territory. The vmPFC-zone peak was *t*(53) = 4.19, below the whole-brain critical *t* = 5.40. Thus, this analysis does **not** support the specific vmPFC hypothesis, although it detects a positive effect elsewhere.
+
+![Group gain-effect results](results/figures/group_gain_effect.png)
+
+## Data and model
+
+We analyzed all 54 equal-indifference participants listed in the supplied cohort table. In this mixed-gambles group, the potential-gain range was twice the potential-loss range. Their maps are unthresholded participant-level gain contrast parameter estimates from AO86, averaged across four runs and reported in MNI152NLin2009cAsym space. All 54 files matched the supplied SHA-256 checksums, had finite values, and shared the same 97 × 115 × 81 voxel grid (2 × 2 × 2.4 mm). No participants were excluded. Because zero-valued voxels denote locations outside a participant’s estimation support, the group test used only the intersection of nonzero map support (198,029 voxels; 1,901 ml); this avoids interpreting absent estimates as observed zero effects. The masks are saved in `results/`. We did not reprocess scans or download time-series data.
+
+At each voxel, we estimated the group mean and a one-sample random-effects *t* statistic across participant contrast estimates, testing the prespecified positive direction. Whole-brain familywise error was controlled with 5,000 participant-level sign-flip permutations of the maximum voxelwise *t* statistic (seed 20261016). The 95th percentile of the permutation maximum distribution was *t* = 5.397. This makes the brain-wide test primary and uses a directional test consistent with the original hypothesis. A finite permutation sample gives a minimum reportable *p* of 1/5,001.
+
+We labeled vmPFC in advance as a medial anterior ventral prefrontal coordinate zone in MNI space (x −20 to 20, y 20 to 60, z −20 to 20 mm). This transparent anatomical approximation only labels the corrected whole-brain result; it does not reduce the number of tested voxels or provide a separate uncorrected ROI claim. The zone contained 7,043 tested voxels. Its mean estimate was −0.00048 (95% *t* interval −0.0143 to 0.0133, in arbitrary contrast-estimate units); its largest voxelwise *t* was 4.19 and none of its voxels passed whole-brain FWE correction.
+
+## Interpretation and limits
+
+The direction of evidence in the vmPFC zone is not sufficient to establish a positive gain response. Failure to pass whole-brain correction is not evidence that the true effect is exactly zero: it means this sample and fixed analysis do not provide sufficiently strong spatially specific evidence under the required whole-brain criterion. The near-zero zone average is descriptive and can conceal spatially heterogeneous effects.
+
+These inputs are contrast estimates, not standardized statistics; upstream gain values were mean-centered and variance-normalized before HRF convolution, so coefficients cannot be read as signal change per currency unit. The individual models used response-time durations and separate gain and loss models, making the estimate conditional on that model and not a direct causal effect of currency value. Individual variance maps and the full upstream executable pipeline are unavailable, so we could not propagate first-level uncertainty through a summary-statistics model or re-evaluate upstream modeling choices. Group inference treats the participant maps as estimates with between-participant variation. The sign-flip max-T method relies on exchangeability/symmetry under the null. The common-support mask is conservative at varying edges and may affect sensitivity. Finally, vmPFC boundaries are not uniquely defined; the coordinate-zone rule is a reproducible approximation, while the primary correction appropriately covers the full brain.
+
+## Reproducibility
+
+Run `python analysis.py --permutations 5000 --seed 20261016` from the workspace root using the supplied Python environment. The script verifies input checksums and writes maps, masks, numerical output, and the figure into `results/`. `analysis_notebook.ipynb` documents and reruns the workflow. `results/results.json` contains the full machine-readable summary and input checksums.
+
+The one-sided, whole-brain inference requirement follows the [NARPS original analysis instructions, Hypothesis 1](https://www.narps.info/files/narps_instructions_for_analysis_teams.pdf), which predicts a positive vmPFC effect for the equal-indifference group and asks teams for whole-brain corrected results. The original NARPS paper likewise states that the hypotheses should be reported from whole-brain rather than ROI-only analyses ([Botvinik-Nezer et al., 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2314-9)).
